base.why: the typed-decisions checkpoint is upstream's choice/noul specialist (0.766 vs 0.362 for the base English checkpoint on typed decisions)

sequence.why: Diablo states are one request, two history lines and an app name, well under 256 tokens; 1024 would only pad

optimisation.why: encoder LR is 2.5x lower than upstream's 2.5e-5: 3,001 training examples is a small domain set and the base must not forget typed decisions; head LR as upstream

rlcd.why: upstream's RLCD settings, unchanged: nothing in Diablo's data argues for different exploration

targets.why: hard gold labels; a little smoothing keeps the proper-scoring reward from pushing logits to extremes before calibration

weighting.why: train intents range from 98 (mission) to 497 (do); square-root balancing lifts rare classes without drowning common ones; hard negatives and safety boundaries are the point of the dataset; one extra shuffled option order per choice item teaches order invariance

model_selection.rule: fewest false-fast, then highest lane accuracy, then highest macro intent accuracy; never training loss
model_selection.save: best epoch only, plus a rolling latest

calibration.method: one temperature per question type (choice, noul) by NLL, on held-out logits
calibration.config: written to rl_agent_config.json temperature; temperature_by_options removed so no inherited bucket can override the fit
calibration.never: the train split, the test split, or test_private
